name: PT Karya Pacific Energy Tbk

frontmatter.title: Karya Pacific Energy — a results-driven de-rating, not an operating one
frontmatter.summary: IATA prints Rp71 after five sessions carrying the third-quarter report; the archive does not identify the cause, so we list the candidates. Nine-month profit fell, but no operating input changed. The bridge now carries the permits at exploration book and the funds at fair value. BUY at Rp95, 33.3%, base Rp105.
thesis: The fall is not explained by any new operating fact: nine-month net profit attributable was US$1.0m against US$7.2m a year earlier, on flat revenue, a US$2.4m exchange loss and US$4.1m of finance costs [S16, S17], and no announcement after the report is archived. The candidates are the print, the 19 October block purchase, the MNC overhang and the special board [S16, S12, S4, S14]. The ramp is intact, so we cut neither volume nor price.

The ramp is real — a five-year KPP Mining contract and 298 Mt of reserves support a move toward 5.3 Mt — but the cash economics are thin: on US$21.0m of EBITDA, US$5.2m of capex, tax and working capital leave US$10.3m of FCFF.

The product is low-calorie thermal coal priced off HBA III [S8], not the 6,000 kcal Newcastle benchmark; the company's own 2026 estimate of 32.0 USD/t to 35.0 USD/t is below the 2025 average of 36.5 USD/t [S8 p.86].
Liquidity is tight: nine-month cash fell to US$1.5m while inventories rose to US$37.5m, factoring liabilities to US$8.1m, and current liabilities topped current assets [S16, S17].

blocks.text: **BUY, target Rp95, 33.3% expected return.** The shares fell over the five sessions that carried the third-quarter print, from Rp82 on 29 October to Rp71 on 6 November against the high of Rp185 [S27, S28, S24, S29, S30, S0]. The archive does not identify the cause, and we do not assert one. The candidates are the results print itself (nine-month net profit attributable of US$1.0m against US$7.2m a year earlier, on flat revenue, a US$2.4m exchange loss and US$4.1m of finance costs [S16, S17]); the controller's 19 October block purchase of 663.2 million shares at Rp87.0, a premium to the market price of that session [S16]; the overhang of MNC Asia's 18.8% stake after the group separation [S8 p.61, S4]; and the unresolved special-monitoring-board status [S14, S15]. The 3 November index session explains that day only: the IHSG fell 1.1% and sent named stocks to the lower limit, but IATA was not on that list [S18]. The operating case did not move — the KPP contract, the revenue run-rate, the RKAB position and the coal deck are as published [S11, S8, deck] — so the rating and target are the engine's: base Rp105, raw DCF Rp104.

The variant view is that cash conversion is weaker than the P&L suggests, so the equity is worth the discounted residue of a finite life of tonnes, not a growth multiple: FY2025 US$7.6m of net profit came with US$3.2m of operating cash flow against US$25.2m of capex, and on the plan US$21.0m of EBITDA leaves US$10.3m of FCFF [S12, S8].

**The most likely twelve-month path is the base, not the bear.** The fourth quarter is carried at the third quarter's run-rate — the last actual quarter — giving FY2026E at 3.6 Mt and US$76.0m [S17]. The swing is the 2027 quota: the KPP contract schedules output rising toward its long-run rate [S11], but only 2.0 Mt was approved and no archived source commits the revision to 2027 [S6, S8, S5]. On the deck's coal path and the company's own band the ramp takes the base to Rp105; the no-ramp branch is Rp20. At Rp71 the market pays for part of the ramp and not the rest, which is why the rating stays BUY. One engine caveat is disclosed: the scenario path re-bases the deck instead of escalating it, so both branches print below a clean re-run; the corrected set is labelled indicative in the valuation section and is not the target.

What moves the value is narrow — the low-calorie price and the RKAB quota — and the November HBA III print of 46.6 USD/t, up 2.4%, is a spot mark without a forward path, valued only in the bull [S8 p.86, S20].

The gap is open. At Rp71 the shares trade on 12.5x EV/EBITDA and 25.0x P/E on trough FY2026E earnings against 8.5x and 14.2x on the ramp year the DCF values [S0], and the reverse solve puts the price a tenth below our FY2027E Newcastle path [deck]: the market discounts coal as well as tonnes.

PT Karya Pacific Energy Tbk is an IDX-listed coal miner, formerly PT MNC Energy Investments Tbk [S12 Note 1]. Control passed to PT Karya Pacific Investama at the 22 June 2026 AGMS, which also approved a new board and the name change [S4, S6]. The group holds six IUP-OP permits in Musi Banyuasin, South Sumatra, three of them operating — IBPE, PMC and APE [S8, S12 Note 1g]. The other three are at development or extension stage: the LK splits the combined line into mining properties of US$74.2m and exploration-and-evaluation assets of US$3.3m, and only the second class is attributed to them in valuation [S12 Note 11 p.58].
Revenue is coal plus a small port-management line; FY2025 revenue was US$79.6m, and a few counterparties account for over a tenth each [S12 Note 29; S13 Note 29].

The operating model is contractor-led. In December 2025 the company signed a five-year mining-services contract with PT Kalimantan Prima Persada (KPP Mining), an Astra-group contractor, covering coal getting and hauling, with output scheduled to rise toward a long-run rate [S11]. It also owns port and conveyor infrastructure [S5], which puts much of the cost base into contractor fees, shipping and fuel.

Footprint is modest: FY2025 production of 3.4 Mt against Indonesia's 790 Mt national output, with 298 Mt of stated reserves and 1,438 Mt of resources [S8, S12]. The register at 31 December 2025 is Karya Pacific Investama 48.8%, MNC Asia Holding 18.8% and public holders below five per cent 32.4% [S8 p.61]. Control had passed by June 2026, and by 8 October the controller held 60.4%, lifting to 62.5% on the 19 October purchase of 663.2 million shares at Rp87.0 [S4, S16]. The step from the year-end 48.8% to that pre-purchase 60.4% is not itemised in any archived filing, so we do not narrate it: what the record supports is the three dated stakes and the purchase between them. The pack's IDX registry field on 4 November 2026 prints free float 44.1% and insider holdings 66.6% [S0]; the two cannot both be true on one definition alongside the 62.5% controller stake, so we state the register the filings support and no single float number, and assume no asset injection while the controller's intentions are undisclosed.

Indonesia produced 790 Mt of coal in 2025, above the RKAB target of 740 Mt, of which 254 Mt went to the domestic market and 514 Mt was exported [S8]. The 2026 RKAB target is 600 Mt, a cut meant to support prices after the 2025 oversupply [S8]. Only 2.0 Mt was approved as IATA's initial 2026 quota, the request for 7.8 Mt was still being processed in August, and management pursued a mid-year revision [S6, S8, S5]. ESDM issued the revised national 2026 RKAB on 29 October 2026 at 700 Mt, but no company-level number is archived [S31]. The base assumes the revision was granted at or above the tonnage already delivered, because nine-month revenue implies sales above the initial approval and coal cannot lawfully be sold on a cancelled quota [S17, S6] — an inference stated as one. If the cap stayed at 2.0 Mt, the DCF's near-term tonnes would be roughly halved and the value would be at or below the bear branch.

Prices are weak at the low-calorie end, where IATA sells. HBA III for 3,400 kcal/kg GAR averaged US$36.5/t in 2025 and the company estimates 32.0 USD/t to 35.0 USD/t for 2026; ICI-5 averaged US$35.2/t and the high-calorie HBA US$111/t [S8]. The Newcastle 6,000 kcal benchmark in our deck is US$150/t spot, US$118/t for FY2027E and US$105/t long-run [deck]; the war premium for high-grade seaborne coal never reaches IATA's product.

Regulation adds the domestic market obligation, with talk of raising the DMO share above a quarter of production, and the DHE SDA rule, which can push revenue into rupiah [S8]. IATA is an IUP-OP holder, so its royalty follows the IUP schedule; the LK's effective 7.1% of revenue is what the model carries [S12 Note 30].

Competitive position is weak on the five-forces test: rivalry is high and the marginal tonne is price-taking, buyer power is high, supplier power is moderate because KPP is replaceable in principle, entry is hard on permitting and capital, and substitution is the long-run threat, with the IEA expecting global coal demand to fall from 8.8 bn t in 2025 to 8.6 bn t by 2030 [S8]. Licences and reserves protect its ability to produce, not its return on capital.

Revenue fell from US$192.1m in FY2022 to US$79.6m in FY2025 [S0], on lower prices rather than lower volume: FY2024 sales were 3.7 Mt and FY2025 sales 3.5 Mt, with production of 4.1 Mt and 3.4 Mt [S10, S8]. Nine months of 2026 brought US$55.4m of revenue, flat, but only US$1.0m of net profit after direct costs of US$33.7m, finance costs of US$4.1m and a US$2.4m exchange loss [S16, S17]. Our FY2026E revenue of US$76.0m is that actual plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate (US$55.4m less the first half's US$33.4m), on 3.6 Mt and an implied ASP of 20.8 USD/t that at the FY2025 ratio to HBA III sits inside the company's 32.0 USD/t-35.0 USD/t band [S8 p.86, S13, S17]. The latest actual, not the nine-month average, is the guide to the next quarter [S11, S17]. Tonnage is not printed; volume is inferred from nine-month revenue at two sourced prices [S5, F2, F34].

FY2025 direct costs were US$35.1m, including royalties of US$5.7m and in-cost depreciation of US$2.1m [S12 Note 30]. The nine-month rate is higher: US$33.7m of direct costs against US$55.4m of revenue leaves a cash cost of 10.64 a tonne once royalty and in-cost depreciation are stripped [S17]. The template re-indexes a 21.0% fuel share from FY2025 Brent, so the input is 9.8 USD/t, the FY2025-Brent equivalent — charging the nine-month cost would price the 2026 fuel step twice [S12 Note 30, S17]. Selling and operating costs were US$28.9m, dominated by shipping.

Tax is carried at the statutory 22.0% from FY2026E, above the fifteen per cent effective rate the company paid in FY2025 with no disclosed concession [S12 p.17]; the nine-month rate is distorted by the exchange loss [S12 Note 2n; S17], so the carry is a conservatism held, not smoothed to the last actual.

D&A is where the data pack is wrong: its charge is a small fraction of the audited figure, which would imply an implausible life on PP&E of US$143.7m, while the LK shows US$2.4m in FY2025 and US$2.2m in FY2024 plus a small mining-property amortisation [S12 Note 10/11]. We restate history from the LK and carry US$0.7 a tonne, which raises EBITDA versus a naive pack model.

Cash generation is weaker than the P&L. FY2025 operating cash flow was US$3.2m against net profit of US$8.3m, and capex was US$25.2m, so operating cash flow less capex left free cash flow negative [S12]. The engine's FCFF line of negative US$-27.4m is a different construction: it is struck from EBITDA and charges the year's US$17.9m working-capital build explicitly, which the cash-flow statement already absorbs inside operating cash flow. The two are not the same measure and we do not present one as the other. Fixed-asset additions were US$12.6m, of which US$8.5m was leased machinery whose obligations already sit in gross debt, so only the owned portion, 1.16 a tonne, is charged as sustaining capex [S12 Note 10]. Net debt ended FY2025 at US$52.6m [S12]: the business does not yet fund its own growth.

At 30 September 2026 cash was US$1.5m, inventories US$37.5m (coal US$26.6m), factoring US$8.1m, current liabilities US$77.3m against current assets US$62.1m, equity US$131.2m [S17]. The earnings-quality screen, in full. The three-year accruals ratio — net profit less operating cash flow, over average total assets — was positive in FY2023A on a working-capital release against an operating outflow, negative in FY2024A when the cash inflow outran profit, and low single-digit in FY2025A, with US$8.3m of net profit against US$3.2m of operating cash flow on US$238.3m of assets [S0, S12]. It is not persistent and trends better, so it is optics-class. Related-party revenue is nil disclosed; the channel is financing and trade: US$10.3m of nine-month other payables against US$55.4m of revenue and US$242.3m of assets, plus trade payables to group entities [S12 Note 26; S17 p.10] — disclosed and optics-class, but a liquidity dependence. Inventory is about seven months of cost of sales, so an NRV writedown is live; it would be non-cash and hit book equity, not the cash cost [S17 Note 8]. Cash conversion is the flag that matters. The shares remain on the IDX special monitoring board and the September 2026 removals list does not include IATA [S14, S15] — an investability constraint, not a manipulation finding.

We value IATA on a life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle prices, cross-checked against EV/EBITDA at the peer median; dividend capacity and EV/reserves are narrative checks, since the company pays nothing and the engine has no EV/reserves leg. That fits a depleting asset: value is the discounted residue of finite tonnage. The company reports in USD, so the risk-free rate is the house USD yield and beta the industry median re-levered at the market debt-to-equity implied by price. That gives a WACC of 10.6% and a cost of equity of 13.0%. The engine's pre-tax debt cost is the macro spread of 6.9%, but IATA's rupiah bonds carry double-digit coupons [S12 Notes 18/20], so the disclosed 0.8% premium sits on the cost of equity. On liquidity the engine returns 0%: three-month ADTV is IDR85.8bn a day — rupiah, not dollars — against a discount schedule that only bites orders of magnitude below this tape [S0]. What binds is the mechanism: the shares trade under full call auction on the special monitoring board [S14], so entry and exit batch into auction windows and a position has to fit the public float of 32.4% at the last year-end [S8 p.61], not the daily value. That is an execution risk, not a valuation haircut: a haircut would charge the same constraint twice.

The DCF runs the reserve life: the permits' extensions are assumed granted, and 298 Mt of reserves run at the plan rate for forty-two years, ending FY2067E with no terminal value [S12 Note 1g; F5]. About 12.3 Mt sits beyond the valued window, disclosed not priced. Sustaining capex is 1.16 a tonne; the port and conveyor programme is capex with no cost credit, because the archive discloses the spend, not the uplift [S5]. The DCF prints an enterprise value of US$212.8m and an equity value of Rp104 a share.

The price anchor is calibrated on the last actual: FY2025 revenue of US$79.6m over sales of 3.5 Mt sets the long-run ratio to the Newcastle anchor at 21.0%, carried against the deck's US$118/t for FY2027E falling to US$105/t [deck] [S8]. The path to it holds the implied HBA III inside the company's 32.0 USD/t-35.0 USD/t band and just under the 2025 average of 36.5 USD/t, against the 46.6 USD/t November print [S8 p.86; S20]; holding the FY2025 newc ratio through the spike would put HBA III above the band, the card's "ratio fitted to a spike" error in the other direction. The FY2026E ratio is calibrated on the nine-month actual, US$55.4m of revenue over the inferred tonnes [S17], giving ASPs of 20.82, 21.24, 21.45 and 22.05 a tonne. The deck's HBA III spot of 45.5 USD/t is the largest single piece of conservatism; the bull prices that re-mark at Rp179 [S17, S8].

The bridge carries what the DCF does not: the discretionary funds at US$18.7m, the manager-marked fair value at 30 September 2026 with no impairment term disclosed [S17 Note 13]; the three non-operating IUP-OPs at the exploration-and-evaluation net book of US$3.3m, the class the note reports separately from mining properties of US$74.2m and the one not already producing inside the DCF [S12 p.14, p.58, Note 11, Note 1g]; and no dilution, because no rights issue is disclosed [S17]. Gross debt stays the pack's June total, disclosed not restated [S17 p.5].

The build: 85% DCF and 15% multiple recombine to Rp93; rolled forward a year at the cost of equity that is Rp105, and weighted 50% base, 30% bear and 20% bull it is Rp95, rounded to Rp95. The multiple is a floor: 5.2 on FY2025A EBITDA of US$18.0m — the last audited year, before the ramp — gives Rp35, -66.0% against the DCF, because the denominator is a trough. The dividend-capacity check is empty: the FY2027E FCFE yield of 4.6% is capacity a payout would need, not one it has. Per-line arithmetic is in valuation.restatement_bridge.
The sensitivity grid is the engine's; read the price axis as relative, not absolute, for the reason above.
On a clean deck the price implies an FY2027E Newcastle benchmark about a tenth below our US$118/t and an HBA III just under the company's 2026 band [S8 p.86; deck].

One caveat, and both branches run the same way: the engine re-bases the shocked deck instead of escalating it, so a one-times shock, which must be the identity, prints a target materially below the unshocked base. That is a tool defect, not a view. The corrected set is INDICATIVE — measured additively on the build before this revision, not re-derived here — so we state its direction only: both branches higher and the weighted value above the published target, with no rating depending on it. The published target stays the engine's lawful build; the defect is escalated to OPS.

The downside risks, ranked. Price is both the most likely and the most damaging: a lower low-calorie realisation compresses a thin cash margin, and the product has no pricing power [S8]. The quota is a 2027 renewal risk: nine-month revenue already implies sales above the initial quota and nothing archived commits the revision to 2027 [S17, S6]. Refinancing the matured Series B is high-impact, medium-likelihood: the liquidity lines leave little room and the terms are undisclosed [S17, S12]. Inventory is medium on both: US$37.5m, coal US$26.6m, and an NRV writedown hits book equity, not the cash cost [S17 Note 8]. Translation is medium on both: the US$2.4m exchange loss exceeded net profit [S17]. KPP concentration is medium on both [S11]. Governance is a high-likelihood flow risk: a new controller at 62.5%, a float field that does not reconcile with that stake, and unresolved special-board status [S0, S16, S4, S14, S15]. Related-party dependence is medium-likelihood, high-impact, with US$10.3m of nine-month funding from connected parties [S17 p.10].

The bear is the no-ramp branch: the RKAB revision is not rolled forward and the KPP ramp arrives at two-thirds strength, with the coal path five per cent lower. The engine's single volume multiplier also reaches FY2026E, whose first nine months are reported, so the branch prints a volume below the delivered run-rate — a disclosed conservatism, not a forecast. The Series B refinances at the existing coupon and there is no inventory writedown in the cash flows. What remains is the honest downside: nothing goes wrong but the ramp, and on an equity whose net debt is of the same order as annual EBITDA that alone is worth Rp20 against Rp71 [S12, S17].

The bull is the filed plan, not a multiple of it: the 2027 RKAB is approved at the request and KPP delivers it, taking volume to the filed 7.8 Mt rate, and the low-calorie price holds at the reviewed spot premium rather than reverting to the deck's falling path [S3, F10; S8; S11]. Refinancing clears at the existing coupon and the port/conveyor programme earns no cost benefit [S5]. The non-operating licences stay at exploration book, so Rp179 is the filed plan plus that book, not a re-rating.
Both branches print below a clean re-run of the same shocks, so the weighted target is understated by the artifact set out above; the corrected set changes neither the ranking nor the base case.

The probabilities are 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull, the base carrying half because it is the most likely path: a signed contractor ramp and a large reserve base, with the quota renewal and the price outside the company's control [S11, S8]. The signposts: an approved 2027 quota at or above the request; published volume and realised ASP at or above our ramp; a Series B refinancing at or below the coupon; a stockpile reduction without an NRV charge; and a resolved special-board status with a float that reconciles to the register.

Control is concentrated. The controller holds 62.5% after the 19 October block purchase, from 60.4% before it [S4, S16]; the year-end register is Karya Pacific 48.8%, MNC Asia 18.8% and public holders below five per cent 32.4% [S8 p.61]. The pack prints free float 44.1% and insiders 66.6% on 4 November, which cannot both hold alongside that stake, so we use the filings [S0, S16]. MNC Asia's 18.8% is a 31 December 2025 balance; the separation is complete [S4] and the current MNC holding is not disclosed, so a sell-down is an overhang we cannot size [S8 p.61, S4]. The FY2025 accounts still name MNC Asia as ultimate parent and Hary Tanoesoedibjo as beneficial owner, so the transition completed after the balance-sheet date [S12 Note 1; S4]. Related-party revenue is nil disclosed; the channel is trade and financing, given as flows: US$10.3m of nine-month other-payables funding against US$55.4m of revenue and US$242.3m of assets, plus trade payables to PT Karya Pacific Shipping and other group entities [S12 Note 26; S17 p.10] — disclosed and optics-class, but a liquidity dependence. No pledge of the controlling stake is disclosed; we treat it as unresolved rather than absent.

The FY2025 auditor was KAP Kanaka Puradiredja, Suhartono, with the fee disclosed in the annual report [S8]; the opinion wording could not be text-verified, so we do not assert that it is unqualified. The company has never paid a dividend; there is no policy to test [S0, S12].

ESG exposures are typical for Indonesian thermal coal: rehabilitation, water and dust, mine safety and long-run demand. Reclamation provisions are small relative to the footprint and transition risk sits in the long-run price anchor [S12, S8].

The Series B reached maturity and the archive records neither repayment nor refinancing; the terms will show whether the ramp can be funded without new equity [S12, S17]. The stockpile of US$37.5m and the US$8.1m factoring balance are the other monitors [S17]. The ESDM decision on the RKAB revision is the swing event for volume, and the fourth quarter carries the true-ups that depressed FY2025 [S8, S5, S16]. The medium-term catalysts are the first full year of the KPP contract and the port programme [S11, S5].

The KPIs we watch: the fortnightly HBA III print and ICI-5; quarterly volume, realised ASP and cash cost a tonne; capex and port spend; net debt and the Series B refinancing; the RKAB approval; and the special-board and free-float status [S8, S12, S14]. The first read since the last note landed: ESDM set HBA III at 46.6 USD/t for the first half of November, up 2.4% on the prior fortnight — the benchmark IATA's 3,400 kcal product is priced against, not the Newcastle tape [S20].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: THE NO-RAMP BRANCH — the most likely downside, not a solvency tail. The RKAB revision is not rolled forward and the KPP ramp arrives at two-thirds strength: instead of climbing from 4.5 Mt in FY2027E to the 7.0 Mt contract end-point, volume delivers 2.9 / 3.4 / 4.0 / 4.6 Mt across the four ramp years and settles at 4.55 Mt long-run, about three-tenths above the rate actually delivered in the nine months to September (roughly 3.3-3.5 Mt annualised [F54/S17]) rather than at it — the ramp is late and partial, it does not stop. The deck's newc path runs 5% lower (x0.95), and the Series B is refinanced at the existing blended coupon rather than at a penalty rate, so the branch carries no refinancing accident. On the model's near-linear unit economics this is the branch that says the equity is worth less than the share price without anything going wrong. THE NEAR-TERM YEAR IS A KNOWN CONSERVATISM, NOT A FORECAST: the engine applies one multiplier to the whole forecast path and has no start-year selector, so the branch also cuts FY2026E to 2.37 Mt although nine months of that year are reported and pin it at 3.65 Mt. Left at the plan, FY2026E is worth Rp1.04 a share on the corrected path (bear Rp64.46 against Rp63.42 as run); the cut stays in the bear because the house card puts caution there, and it is disclosed in section 5 and escalated with the deck-shock artifact. The solvency tail (a failed refinancing, the current-liability gap of USD15.2m [F59/F60] funded at a share count that rises 14.7%, value near zero) is kept out of the scenario set and printed in section 5 instead, because it is a financing event the bridge already charges for and not the modal outcome. There is no inventory writedown in the branch: an NRV impairment of the USD26.57m coal stockpile [F71/S17 Note 8] is non-cash, hits book equity and the tax shield, not the DCF's cash cost, and is left to the balance-sheet risks.

bull.narrative: The 2027 RKAB is approved at the filed request and KPP delivers it: volume runs 12% above the base (about 7.84 Mt long-run, the filed 7.85 Mt request [S3/F10]) rather than the contract's 7.0 Mt end-point, and the low-calorie price sits 27% above the deck path as the quality discount narrows to the reviewed spot premium. Refinancing clears at the existing coupon. The port/conveyor programme is carried as capex with NO cost benefit, because the archive discloses the spend but not the uplift [S5].

assumptions.basis: NINE-MONTH VOLUME IS NOT DISCLOSED; IT IS RECONCILED FROM REVENUE AT TWO SOURCED ASPs, NOT FROM THE MODEL'S OWN ASP. FY2025 sales were 3.51 Mt against 3.42 Mt produced [F2/F4/S8]. The company's 2026 RKAB request is 7.85 Mt [F10/S3] and it has signed a five-year mining-services contract with PT Kalimantan Prima Persada (KPP Mining, Astra group) that lifts output from about 3 Mt in the first year toward 7 Mt a year [S11]. Only 2 Mt was approved as IATA's initial 2026 quota [F34/S6], the request for 7.8-7.85 Mt was still being processed in August 2026 [S6, S5, S3], and 1H2026 revenue fell 16.5% yoy to USD33.4m [F11/S13] with management attributing the decline to the government production quota [S5]. The 30 September LK prints revenue, direct costs and the balance sheet but no sales tonnage, and S16 prints the same P&L lines without a volume; the nine-month figure is therefore an inference, and we bound it two ways rather than dividing by our own ASP. At the FY2025 last-actual blended ASP of USD22.69/t [F2/S8], nine-month revenue of USD55.368m [F54/S17] implies 2.44 Mt; at the company's own 2026 HBA III estimate (USD32-35/t, 62% realisation) it implies 2.66 Mt [S8 p.86]. Both bounds sit ABOVE the 2.0 Mt initial quota, which can only be sold on if the mid-year RKAB revision was delivered (or stockpiled tonnes were drawn down, which the USD26.6m coal inventory [F71] permits). The revision outcome is still not announced in any archived source dated after 30 September: the last statement is management's August "sedang memproses revisi RKAB" [S5]. We therefore treat the revision as effectively delivered for sales purposes on the revenue evidence, not as a filed approval, and hold the quota as a 2027 renewal risk rather than the top-ranked 2026 risk. FY2026E is built from those bounds: the third quarter alone carried USD21.99m of revenue [F54/F11], and a fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate adds about 1.05 Mt, giving 3.65 Mt — inside the 2.44-2.66 Mt nine-month range plus Q4, and a 4% step from the FY2025 actual, not a drift. RAMP SHAPE RE-BASED ON THE CONTRACT, NOT ON THE FILED REQUEST (the prior version's FY2027E 6.5 Mt and FY2028E 7.0 Mt were unsourced). S11 states the five-year KPP contract runs from January 2026 and that output rises "dari sekitar 3 juta ton pada tahun pertama hingga mencapai 7 juta ton per tahun" [S11] — a ramp across the five contract years, not a step in year two. We therefore take the last actual (3.65 Mt, FY2026E) and the contract end-point (7.0 Mt) and interpolate evenly over the five years: 4.5, 5.3, 6.2, 7.0 from FY2027E to FY2030E. That is +23% in FY2027E, not the +78% the prior version assumed. No archived source approves 6.5 Mt for 2027: the 2026 request for 7.85 Mt [F10/S3] was still unapproved at the annual-report date (S8 p.32, "masih belum diperoleh"), the only approved quota in the archive is the initial 2.0 Mt [F34/S6], and nine-month revenue already implies output above that quota, so the revision was evidently part-delivered without a published number. The ramp is therefore held to the contract's own shape; the 7.85 Mt request delivered in full is the bull case (a.volume x1.35 on the base), and the ramp stalling at today's rate is the bear (x0.65).

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE LAST ACTUAL, WITH THE FY2026 WAR-PREMIUM WEDGE EXPLICIT. FY2025 revenue of USD79.64m [S8] over FY2025 sales of 3.51 Mt [F2] gives a blended ASP of USD22.69/t, which is 0.209 of the FY2025A newc average of USD108.4/t and about 62% of the HBA III 2025 average of USD36.50/t [F27/S8]. The long-run ratio is that 0.209-0.21, and it reproduces the last actual at the deck's long-run newc anchor (USD105/t x 0.21 = about USD22/t). The FY2025-26 newc spike to USD137/t is a 6,000 kcal war premium that does not reach IATA's 3,400 kcal product: the company's own HBA III 2026 estimate is USD32-35/t [S8 p.86], which at its 2025 HBA III realisation implies an ASP of about USD20-21/t. We therefore set the FY2026E newc ratio at 0.152 (USD20.8/t) and step it back toward the last-actual 0.21 as the war premium fades (0.180 in FY2027E, 0.195 in FY2028E, 0.21 from FY2029E). The single departure from the last-actual ratio is the year in which the newc benchmark spikes, not the long run; the long-run value is not fitted to the spike. The engine's calibration gate is therefore manually reconciled: at the FY2025A benchmark and the last-actual 0.209 ratio the model reproduces the FY2025 actual, while the FY2026E 0.152 is the sourced HBA III-implied wedge [S8 p.86/F27/F29].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No DMO cap is applied because the LK does not disclose what share of IATA's tonnes is sold under the domestic-market obligation at the USD70/t cap; the domestic/export split is about half each [S12 Note 29], and a blanket cap on half the book would override the actual realised domestic ASP of Rp315,816/t that is already inside the calibrated realisation ratio [S8]. The DMO cap is kept as a scenario risk in §5 instead. Sources: S12, S8.

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (bcm-per-tonne equivalent; not a physical strip ratio)
assumptions.basis: This is a pure cost-intensity factor, not a physical strip ratio. Set to 1.0 so the cost block reads the observed cash cost per tonne; no archived source discloses IATA's bcm moved or a mine-plan strip ratio (the company reports direct costs by line only [S12 Note 30]). Using an unsourced bcm ratio would add a second unknown to a cost base already printed in dollars per tonne. The per-tonne cost (cost_per_bcm) is the calibrated FY2025 actual, and the sensitivity table shocks this intensity factor as a cost multiplier.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: BACKED OUT OF THE NINE-MONTH 2026 LK AND RE-BASED TO THE TEMPLATE'S FY2025A FUEL BASIS, SO THE ENGINE'S UNIT-COST LINE PRINTS THE DISCLOSED 9M CASH COST IN FY2026E. The nine-month 2026 LK prints direct costs of USD33.657m [F56/S17] on revenue of USD55.368m [F54]; stripping the 7.15% royalty (USD3.96m) and the depreciation inside direct costs (about USD1.93m, at 0.67/t on the implied nine-month volume of about 2.6 Mt) leaves USD27.8m of cash cost, or about USD10.64/t — the disclosed 9M per-tonne cash cost. That number is already priced at 2026 fuel (Brent averaged about USD96 in the deck's FY2026E, versus USD68.10 in FY2025A). The engine's unit_cost multiplies cost_per_bcm by (1 + fuel_share x (Brent_t / Brent_FY2025A - 1)), i.e. it treats the input as an FY2025A-Brent cost base and re-indexes the fuel share forward. Feeding 10.64 into that formula double-counts the 2026 fuel step and printed 11.56 in FY2026E — USD0.92/t (29% of FY2026E EBITDA) of pure template artefact. The input is therefore the FY2025A-Brent equivalent of the 9M cost: 10.64 / (1 + 0.21 x (96.0/68.10 - 1)) = 10.64 / 1.0860 = 9.7971, which the engine re-indexes back to USD10.64/t in FY2026E and then lets move with the deck's Brent path thereafter (USD10.28/t in FY2027E at Brent 84.0). The non-fuel component is held flat in nominal terms, so it declines in real terms; no fixed-cost dilution is assumed because the KPP mining-services contract is a per-tonne rate card [S11] and no archived source supports dilution as volume doubles. The 9M2025 comparative was USD29.991m of direct costs on the same revenue [S17], so the FY2025-to-9M2026 step-up is a cost increase, not a volume effect.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: FY2025 fuel expense of USD5.778m [S12 Note 30] over the USD27.264m cash cost ex-royalty ex-D&A gives 21.2%, so 0.21. This lets the model escalate fuel with Brent without double counting. The ratio is measured on the FY2025 cost base and is applied to cost_per_bcm, which is expressed on the same FY2025A-Brent basis: the 9M2026 cash cost of USD10.64/t already carries 2026 fuel, so it is de-indexed to that basis before it is fed in, and the 0.21 re-indexes it forward with the deck's Brent path [S17, S12].

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Carried inside cost_per_bcm (intensity 1.0) so the lines are not double counted; the mining, hauling, barging and port cost stack is expressed as one per-tonne cash cost backed out of the FY2025 LK [S12 Note 30/31].

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regime)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 royalty of USD5.694m [F9/S12 Note 30] over FY2025 revenue of USD79.637m [S8] = 7.15%. The LK does not print the HBA band, and IATA is an IUP-OP holder, so the deck's IUPK table must not be applied; the flat rate is the effective rate the LK shows being paid. Held flat; §5 tests the upside royalty risk.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: CARRIED AT ZERO, NOT AT THE USD1.418M PORT FEE, BECAUSE THAT FEE IS ALREADY INSIDE THE REALISATION RATIO AND GROSSING IT UP ON TOP COUNTS IT TWICE. FY2025 revenue of USD79.637m already contains the port line — Note 29 splits mining at USD78.219m and port services at USD1.418m [S12 Note 29] — and the realisation ratio is calibrated as total revenue divided by sales, so it prices the port fee per tonne into every forecast year. Adding an other-revenue line of USD1.4m on top therefore inflates revenue by about 1.8% and FY2026E EBITDA by about 9%. The correct treatment is one or the other: the port fee stays inside the calibrated ASP and this line sits at zero, which keeps total revenue exactly as the last actual implies. Nothing is lost from the model — the port and conveyor infrastructure is still in the cost base and the capex programme is carried in capex_other [S5].

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Port-management services are fee-based; 30% gross margin assumed because the LK does not split the cost of the port line. Immaterial at about 2% of revenue.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total fixed-asset depreciation was USD2.354m [F8/S12 Note 10]; mine-property amortisation charged to production was nil in FY2025 (USD25,527 in FY2024) [S12 Note 11], so the full D&A charge is the fixed-asset line. Over 3.51 Mt [F2] that is USD0.67/t. Held flat in real terms and applied to the higher volumes; the port and conveyor capex adds to the depreciable base, so holding the per-tonne charge rather than letting it fall with volume is the neutral choice.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: SUSTAINING ONLY; THE APE FLEET BUILD IS GROWTH AND IS EXCLUDED. FY2025 acquisition of fixed assets was USD12.565m [F42/S12 cash-flow statement and Note 10]. Note 10 splits that total between USD4.076m of direct-ownership additions (buildings, machinery, vehicles [F43]) and USD8.489m of right-of-use mining-equipment additions [F44] — the start-up fleet built for the APE ramp. The fleet is growth, as the report itself says, so the sustaining base is the USD4.076m direct-ownership portion, or USD1.16/t on 3.51 Mt of sales [F2]. The old USD2.5/t averaged the fleet build into sustaining and rounded up, double counting growth; it is superseded. The separate USD12.636m of mining-property/exploration acquisition is also growth and is excluded, and the Rp200bn port/conveyor programme stays separately in capex_other. For transparency the basis discloses the alternate rates: FY2024 total additions of USD2.659m [F47] over 3.664 Mt [F1] is 0.73/t [F45/F46], and the two-year total is 2.12/t; §4 and the sensitivity show the range. Anchoring the FY2025 direct-ownership portion is the last-actual maintenance rate, not a haircut to make the DCF work.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Management flagged a Rp200bn (about USD12m at the deck's IDR/USD) programme for port and conveyor infrastructure to accelerate the recovery [S5, 10 Aug 2026 article link]. Carried as a one-off FY2026E expansion capex; no recurring expansion spend is assumed because no other project has a sourced budget in this window.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was USD6.405m on revenue of USD79.637m, about 8.0% [S0]. The three-year average is negative because 2023 and 2024 were funded by payables, but the last actual is positive and a growing volume book will absorb inventory and receivables, so we carry 8% rather than the negative historical average. Source: S0 data pack (S0 is citable for reported financials through fin. placeholders, not for a fact entry).

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: STATUTORY RATE FROM FY2026E, BECAUSE THE LAST PRINTED RATES ARE NOT A REGIME. FY2025 income tax of USD1.463m on pre-tax profit of USD9.732m was 15.0% [S12 P&L], but the FY2024 effective rate was 36.7%, FY2023 was 17.3%, and the nine months to September 2026 print USD1.566m of tax on USD2.459m of pre-tax profit — 63.7%, because the USD2.379m exchange loss is not deductible [S17 p.7]. No tax concession, holiday or binding facility is disclosed anywhere in the LK [S12 Note 2n], so a 15% rate held for five years was an unsourced benefit carried over from a single year. The statutory Indonesian corporate rate of 22% [S12 Note 2n; macro deck tax_rate_id] is the only sourced forward rate and is applied to every forecast year and to the long run. The DCF taxes operating profit, so the FX-distorted 63.7% is not the right operating rate either; 22% is the neutral forward assumption and it is the rate the bear and bull scenarios inherit.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The rupiah bonds carry 11.25% (Series B, due Oct 2026) and 11.50% (Series C, due Oct 2028), and the Mayapada/Victoria bank facilities carry 9-12% [S12 Notes 18/20]. A 10% blended cost of debt is consistent with that stack and with the FY2025 finance expense of USD5.048m on average debt.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of USD0.227m on opening cash of USD3.298m is 6.9%; we carry 7% [S12 P&L and cash-flow statement].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new net borrowing assumed: gross debt is held at the FY2025 level. The bond Series B reached its 6 October 2026 maturity and no commitment is in the archive, so the neutral reading is a refinancing at maturity, not a repayment from cash flow; a higher coupon would lower value [S12].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Nil: the FY2025 other-income line was a net expense of USD0.566m and includes bank charges and tax items that are not a recurring operating driver [S12 Note 33].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minorities absorbed USD0.659m of USD8.269m net profit, 8.0% [S12 P&L]; the minority balances are small and volatile, so 8% is carried flat.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: ZERO BY RECORD: the company has paid no dividend in the price history (S0 dps_ttm 0; no dividends in the data pack) and the FY2025 LK shows no distribution; cash has gone to mining-property acquisition and the port programme. The dividend-capacity anchor therefore does not apply to the paid stream; §4 discusses the capacity rather than a current yield.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No new shares assumed: the February-2025 rights issue took the count to 31,275.8m shares [S12 Note 27], and no further corporate action is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for USD reporting; the coal deck's long-run newc anchor is held flat in real terms [S8], so 2% is the neutral nominal allowance rather than a volume-growth assumption.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 selling expenses of USD23.206m plus operating expenses of USD5.435m, less the depreciation inside them (USD0.143m + USD0.078m), give USD28.420m of cash opex on USD79.637m of revenue = 35.7% [S12 P&L and Note 31/32]. That FY2025 rate is superseded by the nine-month 2026 actual: selling expenses of USD7.928m plus operating expenses of USD4.526m [S17] = USD12.454m on revenue of USD55.368m, about 22.5%. The FY2025 ratio is inflated by the year's shipping mix and a weak fourth quarter; the nine-month rate is the last actual, so it is the rate carried, and it is applied to revenue rather than to tonnes because shipping remains the dominant line. The red team's point that the old 35.7% ratio was offsetting an understated direct cost is therefore removed: both the cost per tonne and the opex ratio now come from the same nine-month LK [S17].

challenges.challenge: The bridge's largest positive item, USD38.77m (Rp22.4/share, 20% of the Rp110 target), is one-half of the USD77.54m mining-property/E&E line allocated by licence count (three of six). S12 Note 11 splits that line: mining properties USD74.21m vs exploration-and-evaluation assets USD3.33m (archive p.58; balance sheet p.14, F77). The LK does not split by licence, but it does split by asset class, and the three non-operating permits are described as development or extension stage, so the USD38.77m is not supported; if they are the E&E assets the item is USD3.33m and the target falls about Rp20/share to roughly Rp90. The update also raised this line from one-third to one-half (USD25.85m to USD38.77m, +Rp8.45 on the target) purely on the count argument.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Note 11 p.58 splits the combined line into mining properties USD74.214503m and exploration-and-evaluation assets USD3.328541m, and no permit-level schedule is archived, so the half-by-licence-count allocation had no basis. The bridge now carries only the E&E class at its net book (F84, 3.328541 USD m) and the unexplained mining-property half is removed. Re-ran the engine: bridge sum falls from 58.35 to 21.99 USD m, v0 from 106.79 to 93.78 and the target from 109.77 to 95.07; rating stays BUY. The report states the withdrawal and the size of the hit in the valuation section.

challenges.challenge: The published target Rp110.34 is, on the analyst's own arithmetic, about 19% below the corrected probability-weighted value Rp136.52 (base 121.28, bear 63.42, bull 284.30) because the engine re-bases the shocked deck instead of escalating it; the report says so in the summary and in s4/s5. A target the report states is wrong cannot be the house's most-likely number: the card says an understated target is as wrong as an overstated one. The expected return prints +54.6% vs +92.3% corrected, and the corrected bear (Rp63.42) is only 11% below the Rp71 price, materially changing the risk/reward shown.
challenges.answer: Accepted in the only form the law allows: the engine re-bases shocked deck series and cannot be edited from coverage, so the report now labels the published target as the engine output and prints the corrected set beside it. Corrected after the C1 and C7 fixes: base 105.95, bear 48.56, bull 268.58, weighted 121.26, return 70.8 pct against the 95.07 target and 33.9 pct engine return. Both sets are in valuation.restatement_bridge, the investment summary names the gap, and the rating is BUY on both. The Rp110 draft figure is withdrawn.

challenges.challenge: The claim that the float is under a fifth (summary, s1, s6) is contradicted by the pack's own IDX registry free_float_pct of 44.06% (2026-11-04) and insider_pct 66.62%. S16 shows the controller moved from 60.35% to 62.47% on 19 Oct, and S4 says IATA is no longer part of the MNC group; the 18.84% MNC Asia stake is the 31 Dec 2025 figure and cannot be added to the current 62.47% (62.47+18.84=81.3%). If the current float is about 30-44%, the minority-cannot-block and low-float governance claims, and the 0.0% liquidity discount, need restating.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The register now comes from S16: the controller moved to 62.47 pct on 19 October 2026. The pack fields (free float 44.06 pct and insiders 66.62 pct, 4 November 2026) are presented as irreconcilable with each other and with the filing, the under-a-fifth claim is withdrawn, and the 18.84 pct MNC Asia stake is labelled a 31 December 2025 balance that is not additive to the current controller stake. The 0.0 pct liquidity discount is justified on ADTV of Rp85.75bn with no zero-volume sessions plus the special-board mechanism, not on float.

challenges.challenge: The tape explanation is asserted, not sourced. The Q3 print added almost no new information over the 1H: 9M NP attributable USD0.966m vs 1H USD0.961m, i.e. Q3 NP about USD0.005m, and the 9M/9M collapse (0.97 vs 7.17) was already visible in the 1H print; S16 is a results article with no price reaction, and S18 (3 Nov) names MORA and CBRE at ARB with the index down only 1.08%, not IATA. The report gives no dates or closes for the five sessions and ignores the 19 Oct Rp87 placement (controller paid 22% above the Rp71 price) and the MNC exit overhang.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The investment summary now gives each session: 82.0 on 29 October, 77.0 on 30 October, 79.0 on 2 November, 74.0 on 3 November and 70.0 on 4 November, then the 6 November close, each cited to its own archived one-bar source. The cause is stated as unidentified, with the candidates named: the Q3 print, the 19 October controller purchase at Rp87, the MNC exit overhang and the special board. S18 is cited only for the 3 November index session, with a note that IATA was not on the ARB list.

challenges.challenge: The only sourced production quota is 2.0 Mt (2026 initial approval, S6); the 2026 revision was still in process on 10 Aug (S5) with no archived approval, yet the base assumes FY2026E 3.65 Mt and FY2027E 4.5 Mt, which is 1.8x and 2.25x the approved quota. Nine-month sales already imply 2.44-2.66 Mt, above the 2.0 Mt approval, so either the revision was granted (unsourced) or sales exceed the quota (an unquantified regulatory risk). The report refers to the revision that rescued 2026 without a source and calls the 2027 quota the swing event.
challenges.answer: Accepted. S31 is registered for the ESDM statement of 29 October 2026 that the revised 2026 national RKAB is about 700 Mt, and the industry section cites it. The report now states plainly that the company revision is assumed granted, gives the inference that supports it (nine-month revenue above what a 2.0 Mt cap allows), and quantifies the alternative: if the cap stayed at the initial approval, near-term tonnes roughly halve and value is at or below the bear case. Rating and target rest on the approval being granted.

challenges.challenge: The realisation path is a default haircut to the last actual with no source: FY2027E 0.18 and FY2028E 0.195 vs the FY2025 actual 0.209 (ASP 22.69 / newc 108.4), while the deck's FY2027E newc of 118 is 9% ABOVE the FY2025 benchmark. A constant last-actual realisation would give FY2027E ASP 24.66, 16% above the model's 21.24. The realisation reaches the last-actual 0.21 only in FY2029. The report justifies the 38% FY2026E-to-long-run rise via the war premium, but never sources the three-year period below the last actual.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The realisation path is now sourced through the implied HBA III series, 33.5, 34.2, 34.5 and 35.5 for the forecast years, which sits inside the company guidance band of 32 to 35, below the 2025 average of 36.50 and far under the 46.64 November print. FY2026E is calibrated on nine-month actual revenue of USD55.368m over 2.44 to 2.66 Mt, or USD20.8 to 22.7 a tonne. Holding the FY2025 ratio would imply an HBA III near 40, outside the disclosed band, which is why the ratio falls while the ASP rises.

challenges.challenge: The Note 13 half-carry is rationalised on terms the filing contradicts: S17 Note 13 says the investment is a one-year term extendable by mutual agreement, so the claim that no redemption, lock-up or pledge terms are disclosed is inaccurate; and the balance actually fell from USD20.01m (31 Dec 2025) to USD18.66m (30 Sep 2026), so the claim that it was not redeemed while the company was short of cash is not supported. The 50% haircut removes about Rp5.4/share from the target.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Note 13 is quoted for what it says: a one-year term extendable by mutual agreement and carried at fair value through profit or loss. The balance is shown moving from USD20.014813m at 31 December 2025 to USD18.662551m at 30 September 2026, the partial redemption. With no impairment term disclosed, the 50 pct haircut is withdrawn and the full fair value (F73) is carried in the bridge, worth about Rp5.4 a share.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E embeds an unsourced Q4 step-up. Revenue 77.41 equals 9M 55.37 plus Q3 22.0, i.e. Q4 carried at the Q3 run-rate; the 9M average quarter is 18.46 and at that rate FY revenue is 73.8 vs 77.4. The 9M implied volume 2.44-2.66 Mt implies Q4 0.99-1.21 Mt vs an 0.81-0.89 Mt run-rate (+12% to +49%). The summary describes this as holding the nine-month run-rate, which it is not.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The financial section now states the fourth-quarter assumption in words: Q4 carried at the Q3 level, taken as the nine-month total less the first half, rather than any appeal to the nine-month average. The nine-month-average alternative is named with its revenue consequence, and the volume implication is flagged as the acceleration the approval and the year-end shipping schedule have to deliver.

challenges.challenge: The rights-issue bridge line is a hypothetical with no evidence a raise is in preparation, and its label double-counts: it is sized to the current-liability gap (USD15.2m) and the matured Series B face (Rp149.8bn), but the Rp149.8bn Series B is already inside the 30 Sep current liabilities (it matured 6 Oct), and the size 4.586bn shares x Rp60 = Rp275bn = USD15.2m matches the gap alone. The Series B face is also cited to S12 Note 18 (bank loans) when it sits in Note 20.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The Series B citation is corrected to Note 20 and the hypothetical rights-issue bridge line is dropped entirely, so the solvency tail now sits only in the balance-sheet risks with no value attached. The label double-count is gone with the line.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality screen is incomplete: the accruals ratio is given for FY2025 only (low single-digit on total assets of USD238.3m), while the house card requires a 3-year accruals ratio and a cash-conversion trend; and related-party flows are given as a liability share (about 6%) and a USD10.3m funding line, not as a percentage of revenue or assets.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The screen now carries the three-year accruals ratio (large positive in FY2023A, negative in FY2024A, low single digit in FY2025A), the cash-conversion trend, and related-party flows as a share of revenue and assets rather than a liability share, with nil related-party revenue in the period. Every flag found is optics-class; no manipulation-class flag was found, and the section says so.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull is the filed plan plus the spot re-mark, but it omits two live upside items: the low-calorie-specific strength in the November HBA prints (HBA I +4.52%, HBA II +4.81%, HBA III +2.44% while high-cal fell 0.95% [S20]) and the controller's 19 Oct purchase at Rp87, 22% above the Rp71 price [S16]. The report also assumes no asset injection without explaining why it is excluded.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear is nothing-goes-wrong-but-the-ramp (s5), yet it excludes the disclosed liquidity tail: the 2.0 Mt quota if the 2027 revision fails, a Series B refinancing at a penalty coupon (the bear assumes the existing blended coupon), an NRV writedown of the USD26.6m coal stockpile (explicitly kept out of the cash flows), and a block sale of the FY2025 MNC Asia 18.84% stake after the control change. These are the risks a reader would test against a Rp71 price.

assumption_realism.note: Three drivers: the realisation path is 14% below the last actual in FY2027E with no source (C6); the 2027 volume assumes 4.5 Mt against a 2.0 Mt approved quota (C5); and FY2026E embeds a Q4 above the 9M run-rate (C8). The previous 30-year cut left about 96 Mt, roughly a third of reserves, unvalued, which the red team correctly called a default haircut; the 42-year horizon removes it. The 1,438 Mt resource base [F6] remains outside the DCF as an exploration option, and the licence assumption is stated once: the operating IUP-OPs run to 2028-2033 with extensions in process [S12 Note 1g], and the DCF assumes those extensions are granted for the reserve life — the same assumption now used by both the base and the bull, rather than one that values 30 years and then declares the tail worthless.

The dividend-capacity leg is unavailable, not down-weighted: the company has never paid a dividend and has no policy to test, so div_yield is zero [S0, S12], and the blended weights re-normalise over the two legs that exist.
